name: Toyota Celica GT-Four (ST205)
engine: 2.0L turbocharged I4 (3S-GTE) with the twin-entry CT20b turbo, ~239 hp (export) / 252–255 PS (JDM)
drivetrain: AWD (full-time, with a Torsen center differential)
fuel_economy: Not US-EPA rated (JDM/Euro homologation car); real-world ~20–24 mpg
reliability: 8/10 — the ST205 is a rally homologation special built in strictly limited numbers (about 2,500 to satisfy Group A WRC rules), so it is rarer and more specialized than a normal Celica. Mechanically the 3S-GTE turbo four is proven and strong, but this version runs more boost and hardware — the water-to-air intercooler, the twin-entry CT20b turbo, and a genuine AWD driveline — all of which need care on a car now 30 years old. The bigger ownership challenge is parts: many GT-Four-specific and homologation pieces are scarce and expensive. A well-maintained example is a special, appreciating collector car.
cost_to_own: Insurance: High (rare turbo-AWD collector/import) · Maintenance ~$800/yr and rising with parts scarcity · A genuine appreciating homologation special — provenance, originality, and a documented history drive value
popular_mods: A front-mount intercooler upgrade — the factory water-to-air setup heat-soaks under sustained load
A boost controller and supporting fueling for a safe, modest power bump on the stout 3S-GTE
Refreshed AWD driveline service (center diff, couplings) — keep the rally hardware healthy
Suspension refresh with quality dampers to restore the rally-bred handling
Honest take: originality is the value here — a light, reversible tune and meticulous maintenance beat heavy modification on a homologation car
oil_interval: Every 3,000–5,000 miles (shorter on a hard-driven turbo)

generations.ST205 (1994–1999): The final and most focused Celica GT-Four. Built to homologate the car for Group A World Rally Championship (~2,500 units), it added the twin-entry CT20b turbo, water-to-air intercooling, uprated brakes, a stiffer body, and the rally-derived AWD system. The rare WRC/Group A edition with the 'Super Strut' suspension is the collector's pick.
generations.Lineage note: It followed the ST165 (1986–1989) and the celebrated ST185 (1990–1993), the generation that won Toyota's WRC titles. All three GT-Fours pair the 3S-GTE turbo with full-time AWD; the ST205 is the last and most hardcore.

common_issues: Parts scarcity — many GT-Four-specific and homologation components are hard to find and costly
Aging turbo and water-to-air intercooler system that heat-soaks under sustained boost
AWD driveline wear (center differential, viscous coupling) on high-mile or hard-used cars
Rust on a 30-year-old body, especially on cars from salt climates — inspect thoroughly
Grey-import complexity in some markets (age exemptions, parts sourcing, service knowledge)
maintenance_tips: Service the AWD driveline and check the center diff/coupling — the rally hardware is core to the car
Address turbo and intercooler heat management before pushing boost on the aging system
Use good synthetic oil on a short interval and let the turbo warm up and cool down
Inspect the body carefully for rust and prior accident/rally history before buying
Preserve originality and paperwork — provenance is what makes a genuine ST205 valuable

engine.detail: 2.0L turbocharged 3S-GTE four with the twin-entry CT20b turbo and a water-to-air intercooler — ~239 hp in export trim, 252-255 PS JDM. The 3S-GTE bottom end is proven and stout.
engine.watch: The aging turbo and water-to-air intercooler heat-soak under sustained boost — sort cooling and heat management before pushing boost, and always warm up and cool down the turbo.

drivetrain.detail: Full-time all-wheel drive with a Torsen center differential and viscous coupling, driven through a 5-speed manual — genuine rally-derived hardware.
drivetrain.watch: The center diff and viscous coupling wear on high-mile or hard-used cars; service the driveline regularly, and be aware many GT-Four-specific parts are scarce and expensive.

suspension.detail: Rally-bred strut suspension, stiffened over lesser Celicas; the rare WRC/Group A edition adds the sought-after 'Super Strut' front setup.
suspension.watch: Refresh dampers and bushings to restore the handling — Super Strut components in particular are hard and costly to source.

brakes.detail: Uprated four-wheel discs over the standard Celica, with ABS, to match the homologation car's pace.
brakes.watch: GT-Four-specific brake parts fall under the same scarcity problem — budget for the hunt on a 30-year-old collector car.

body.detail: A stiffer, homologation-spec Celica shell built in roughly 2,500 units to satisfy Group A World Rally Championship rules.
body.watch: Rust is the big one on a 30-year-old body, especially salt-climate cars — inspect thoroughly and check for prior accident or rally history; grey-import examples add sourcing and service complexity.
